newsitem.title: UGANDA: Forty Ugandans reported killed in rebel incursion.
newsitem.headline: Forty Ugandans reported killed in rebel incursion.

text.p: At least forty civilians have been killed by rebel forces who invaded an area of western Uganda last week from the neighbouring Democratic Republic of the Congo (formerly Zaire), residents fleeing the area said on Sunday.
They said fighting continued on Saturday around the small town of Bundibugyo -- cut off from the rest of Uganda by a spur of the Ruwenzori mountain range.
The only road connecting Bundibugyo with the rest of Uganda was under attack.

Armed supporters of the Allied Democratic Forces (ADF), a small rebel group which launched attacks on nearby areas earlier this year, looted Bundibugyo after overrunning a small army post on the border last Monday.
The government-owned New Vision newspaper in Kampala reported that over 200 rebels had been killed in fighting with the Uganda army.
An estimated 12,000 civilians have fled their homes in the area, and there is a serious shortage of food there, the paper added.
Ugandan defence minister Amama Mbabazi told Reuters on Sunday: "We are carrying out mopping-up operations around Bundibugyo. There have been casualties."
Residents fleeing the area said the ADF rebels were heavily armed, and supported by members of the former Rwandan army, who were driven out of their country after a wave of genocide there in 1994.
Ugandan officials describe the ADF as a small dissident group which has previously carried out sporadic attacks in other border areas.

They had been operating from bases in western Congo for some months, they said, but now appeared to have been reinforced after linking up with remnants of the former Rwandan army, and with members of the recently-defeated Zairean army.
Ugandan President Yoweri Museveni met his top army commanders in Western Uganda last week to discuss operations against the ADF rebels.
